blockingFindings: SP01.2 collapses the RP01 subset gates. openspec/sprints/sprints.json assigns the same task SP01.2 to rp01-mc02, rp01-mc03, and rp01-full, and openspec/sprints/sp01-financial-contract-and-execution-admission.md SP01.2 verify requires a complete RP01 map with no missing design row. There is no partial-completion protocol, so rp01-mc02/rp01-mc03 cannot close independently. That forces SP05 (i2) and SP06 (f2) to wait for the full challenge map, contradicting openspec/sprints/README.md (SP04/SP05/SP06 do not wait for full RP01) and openspec/REPORT-RECONCILIATION-2026-09-07.md subset admission. openspec/sprints/verify.py allows one task in multiple entryGates and does not catch this. Split SP01.2 into separately closable subset packets versus the full map.

Native command trees are already forked, and the promised freeze is not on the native entry path. openspec/changes/mc03-native-recursive-proof/tasks.md still owns experiments/moriarty-native-ivc-r3/revision-01/; SP06 creates experiments/moriarty-native-ivc-r3/successor/; SP04 creates experiments/moriarty-ledger-adapter/probes/. SP01.5 says freeze one command manifest and exact paths before either native writer starts, but sprints.json entryGates do not require SP01.5 (or any path freeze) for f0a, f1-fixtures, f1, or f2. An entryGate-following implementer can author duplicate export/finalizer shims after F0 alone. Make the SP01.5 path/command freeze a hard prerequisite of SP04.1 and SP06.1.
nonblockingFindings: SP09.1 in openspec/sprints/sp09-mandatory-pcd-and-ledger-correspondence.md is one umbrella over MC04 P.1-P.7, atomic K bootstrap, MC04 3.1-3.2, and Preview F3. The charter forbids combining pre-launch review and native execution in one ungated bundle. Pointing at P.1-P.7 is not the same as separate executable packets under openspec/sprints/execution/.

SP07 and SP08 both modify experiments/moriarty-language/formal/k/moriarty.k in parallel (actus-semantics and defi-semantics both require only successor-semantics). Serialization is prose-only in the charter/README; neither sprint names file-level ownership or a merge order.

openspec/sprints/coverage.json taskCrosswalk maps only MC04 P.1-P.7 and 3.1-3.2. MC05/MC06/MC07 P campaigns and remaining MC01-ATOMIC work (tasks.md 2.x frontend, 3.x elaboration, 4.x Compact lowering) have no sprint-task IDs. Implementers can skip atomic Compact/evaluator closure in SP01.1/SP01.5 or dispatch package P-tasks off the stage graph.

SP01.1 checkbox order writes openspec/sprints/execution/SP01.md before inspect/run, while openspec/sprints/README.md requires inspect-before-prescribing the input-boundary fix. Checkbox-driven agents can plan a redundant correction.

Dispatch graphs disagree on mandatory-claims-01. sprints.json mandatory requires actus-semantics and defi-semantics (full SP07/SP08 libraries) before SP09.2-SP09.5, but openspec/moriarty-completion-program.json package MC05 still depends only on MC03 and MC04. That can launch the MC05 native campaign too early or block MC05 package acceptance on full libraries, depending on which graph is followed.

SP01.4 states an at-most-30-minute F0 ceiling that reads as a granted allocation; README and sprints.json resourceAllocationGranted=false say it is not. F0 complete versus F0 go is also not encoded in the stage requires list, so a no-go F0 could still unlock f0a if a scheduler only checks sprints.json.
